quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You need to see clearly through all your windows to drive safely. Clear all snow, ice, and frost from your windows and mirrors before driving.

questions.question: To avoid losing grip on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Make abrupt turns.
Apply the brakes firmly.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads to prevent skidding. Keep your tires in good condition. If you start to skid, take your foot off the gas, do not brake hard, keep the vehicle straight, and let it slow down.

questions.question: To see traffic behind you:

options.text: Frequently check your rearview mirror.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently check your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to know where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: Allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when driving behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one taillight.

questions.question: If you need your lights on while driving in bad weather or low light:

options.text: Use your parking lights.
Use your high beams.
Use your low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beam light reflects back and creates glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle:

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable. Young riders often make sudden direction changes. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to police:

options.text: Only if you are in a crash.
If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. Show your insurance proof and license to an officer when asked after a traffic stop or crash.

questions.question: You have a minor crash with no injuries and little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
Not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: After a crash with no injuries or deaths, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Highway entrance ramp.
Road widens.
Right lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you the right lane is ending and warns you to prepare for cars merging.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and go slowly. Slow down and watch for hazards.

questions.question: A red curb means:

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, park, or stand at a red curb.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Slow down when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has many turns or curves.
More traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you the road will be slippery when wet. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring only at the road directly ahead.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to stay aware of hazards. Do not stare only at the road ahead—it is dangerous. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Turn in that direction after slowing down and checking for traffic.
Do not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
Turn in that direction after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Never turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Stay close to other vehicles to maintain traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, shift to low gear before going downhill. Also stay farther away from the vehicle ahead than normal. Avoid quick stops. Unless you have antilock brakes, pump the brakes to slow down or stop.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.
Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles with sirens and lights pass. Drive to the right edge and stop until the vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first and then stop.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and collision severity change with speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause longer stopping distances and worse collisions. As speed increases, the chance of serious injury and death increases. Increase your following distance as you go faster.

questions.question: When can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes in your direction.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive off the paved road onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: As your speed increases, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At higher speeds, your stopping distance increases. Look far ahead so you have time to safely react to hazards.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
As speed increases, you should increase your following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds greatly increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 mph, survival is unlikely. Increase your following distance as you drive faster because stopping distance increases with speed.

questions.question: When passing a car, when do you have enough space to return to your lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to re-enter.
When you look over your shoulder and see the car behind you.
When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure there is safe distance between your vehicle and the passed vehicle. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use turn signals?

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
Only when parking at the curb.
When parking at or leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parking at or leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signals when parking at a curb and when leaving a curb.

questions.question: Your vehicle loses traction because of water on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to get better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, tires can lose contact with the pavement and ride on water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.

questions.question: What can happen when you take a prescription drug with alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
You will become more alert.
You may become unfit to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may become unfit to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can affect your ability to drive. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When the center line has a solid yellow line on one side and a broken yellow line on the other, passing is allowed from the broken line side and not allowed from the solid line side.
